headlines.title: Westbound I-80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge to close this weekend
headlines.description: A section of westbound Interstate 80 in San Francisco near the Bay Bridge will be closed this weekend for a construction project. The full westbound I-80 closure from Fifth Street to 15th Street is scheduled to start at 11 p.m. Friday and continue until 6 a.m. Monday, according to Caltrans. Motorists should avoid using the Bay Bridge to get into San Francisco during the closure, Caltrans said. Alternate options include taking public transportation or using the San Mateo, Dumbarton or Richmond-San Rafael bridges. “This work is necessary for crews to place polyester concrete on the WB I-80 Bayshore freeway deck and will complete a broader I-80 Bayshore Freeway viaduct polyester concrete placement project which began on the eastbound I-80 Bayshore Freeway earlier this year,” Caltrans said in a statement. The map below provides a closer look at the closure details and detour options.

headlines.title: 71-year-old man dies after being struck by self-driving car on I-80 in Vallejo
headlines.description: A 71-year-old man was killed early Thursday morning after he was struck by a self-driving car as he was crossing Interstate 80 in Vallejo, the California Highway Patrol said. According to the CHP’s Solano-area office, officers were alerted to a collision reported around 2:35 a.m. on westbound I-80 at the I-780 interchange. When they arrived, first responders found the severely injured pedestrian, who was later declared dead. The driver of the involved vehicle, a 26-year-old San Francisco man, stayed at the scene and told CHP officers that his vehicle, a Tesla, was being operated in Full Self-Driving autonomous mode when it hit the pedestrian. According to the CHP, the Tesla had full footage of the crash since it was recorded by the vehicle’s dashcam. Based on the video, the Tesla was traveling around 70 mph when the pedestrian entered the freeway. He began crossing toward the center divider from the right shoulder, placing him directly in front of the Tesla. “The video showed the Tesla’s brakes being applied as the vehicle steered to the left in an effort to avoid the pedestrian. Despite these evasive actions, the right front portion of the Tesla struck the individual,” the CHP said in a statement on social media. The agency said the 71-year-old was again struck by at least one more vehicle while lying in the traffic lanes, adding that no other vehicles stopped to cooperate with authorities. The other involved vehicle or driver is yet to be identified. “The Solano Area CHP extends its deepest condolences to the family and friends of the deceased during this difficult time,” the agency said. Anyone who may have witnessed the crash or who has information regarding the other vehicles involved is encouraged to contact the CHP Solano-area office at 707-639-5600.

headlines.title: Video game developer BioWare shuts down, next ‘Mass Effect' canceled amid broader layoffs at EA
headlines.description: Video game publisher Electronic Arts is shutting down the popular and influential game development studio BioWare after more than three decades. The upcoming “Mass Effect” game, the fifth since 2007, has been canceled. BioWare announced the closure on social media Wednesday following a report by Bloomberg that also said the company is laying off 400 people, including about 50 at BioWare. The Redwood Shores, California-based maker of popular titles like “Battlefield” and “The Sims” closed the $55 billion sale of its business to Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund PIF, investment firm Silver Lake Partners and Affinity Partners, which is run by President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, in August. Representatives for EA did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment on the layoffs. “What generations of BioWare built together is something to celebrate and remember,” the studio said via social media. “These games became so much more because you played them, debated your choices, fell in love with characters, and made these worlds your own.” BioWare built its reputation on immersive role-playing adventures, from sword-and-sorcery fantasies like “Baldur’s Gate” and “Dragon Age” to science fiction epics like “Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic” and “Mass Effect.” But its effort to branch out into multiplayer shooters, 2019’s “Anthem,” steered away from the studio’s strength as a creator of compelling single-player narratives. It failed to find the sort of loyal audience that keeps online hits like “Fortnite” and “Overwatch” humming. Meanwhile the latest installments of its two most popular original franchises — 2017’s “Mass Effect: Andromeda” and 2024’s “Dragon Age: The Veilguard” — met with mixed reviews and disappointed many fans. A new chapter of “Mass Effect” was in development before BioWare announced its shutdown. BioWare, based in Canada, was founded in 1995 and acquired by EA in 2007. __ Associated Press Writer Lou Kesten in Washington contributed.

headlines.title: Federal judge orders Trump administration to halt noncitizen voting investigation in 9 states
headlines.description: A federal judge in California has ordered the Trump administration to halt investigations in nine states into whether noncitizens are registered to vote. U.S. District Court Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin in Oakland found the government’s effort is relying on data that is full of errors and that it’s leading to intimidation of groups performing voter assistance efforts. She said it should be halted until polls close on Election Day, Nov. 3. She put her ruling, which was made Wednesday, on hold until Friday to give the administration a chance to appeal. The ruling applies to investigations in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin. It comes as the Trump administration has been hunting for noncitizen voters throughout the country in the months leading into the midterm elections. The administration has signaled that it’s a major problem, when in fact it’s quite rare, as even its own investigations have shown. The lawsuit was filed by the California Nurses Association and National Nurses United, along with the Voto Latino Foundation, San Francisco and Santa Clara County. In response to the ruling, the Department of Homeland Security issued an email statement Thursday saying it’s focused on “removing aliens who vote and dilute the votes of U.S. citizens,” while adding, “We have no plans to question or investigate people we believe to be U.S. citizens.” According to legal filings in the case, investigators were told to target naturalized citizens to see whether they had voted before they became U.S. citizens. The lists of voters to check came from sources that included state and local governments and publicly available information. Martinez-Olguin called them “voluminous and unreliable.” “Even under the best conditions, there is a high likelihood of error in review because there is no federal database containing citizenship status of U.S. residents,” Martinez-Olguin wrote in her ruling. “The time limitations implemented during the Surge further exacerbate the risk of error.” The Department of Justice has been demanding detailed and unredacted voter roll data from the states and has sued the 30 states that have refused to turn it over, losing each of those cases so far. The judge noted that for states that refused to share their records, the administration was trying to obtain them through “unreliable commercial versions of voter roll data.” She said during a “surge” phase of the investigation starting in late August, agents were ordered to complete reviews of flagged individuals taking no more than 12 minutes per person to assess whether they were legally qualified to vote. In their challenge, the plaintiffs said some U.S. citizens felt they were wrongly identified and investigated as part of the probe. Martinez-Olguin said those fears “are well understood as intimidation” that has chilled people from attending campaign events and working as poll monitors during the election. Beau Tremitiere, a lawyer representing the unions and voter group, said in a statement that the ruling affirms the groups’ position. “It was clear from the start that DHS built its lists on bad data, never checked how often it was wrong, and recklessly sent agents to people’s homes weeks before an election,” Tremitiere said. Details of the investigation, known as the “Unlawful Voter Initiative,” came to light last month after Democratic Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer of New York and Democratic Sen. Alex Padilla of California released a whistleblower report about it.

headlines.title: San Jose community pushes to rebuild MACSA youth center destroyed by fire
headlines.description: A San Jose neighborhood is working to rebuild a center that it says was the heart of the community. The building that once housed the MACSA youth center in the Mayfair community burned to the ground in August of last year. At the time, community members told NBC Bay Area what the center meant to them and their families. Since then, neighbors and activists have been pushing for it to be rebuilt to serve the community. In May, the rebuild was approved by the Alum Rock School District. Somos Mayfair was a major proponent of retaining the cultural aspect of the building that had been shuttered. San Jose City Councilmember Peter Ortiz also lent his voice to the cause. “MACSA center was a safe place for our youth, especially the ones impacted in gangs,” Ortiz said. A MACSA input session will be held Thursday at the Mayfair Community Center from 4:30 to 7 p.m. The session is directed at students and their families, as the goal is to create a youth center that will serve them.

headlines.title: Bay Area voter guide: What to know about the November 2026 election
headlines.description: What to Know — Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026 California will choose a new governor to replace Gavin Newsom, who terms out after this year. The choices are Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton. Voters will decide 14 state propositions. Regional sales tax Measure RTM, the Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, aims to increase funds for public transit. California’s Congressional District 11 race features Scott Wiener and Connie Chan competing to succeed Nancy Pelosi. Aisha Wahab and Melissa Hernandez will face off again after a special election in August where Wahab secured victory to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. All 80 California Assembly seats are up for reelection, as well as 20 Senate seats. California’s general election is Nov. 3, with statewide races and propositions as well as key local races and measures across the Bay Area. Here’s what you need to know to cast your ballot, including important dates and deadlines, how to register or check your status, where and when to vote, and what’s on the ballot. In this guide: Key election dates Check voter registration status How to register to vote How to find your polling place What to bring to your polling place How to track your mail-in ballot Why is California choosing a new governor? 14 California propositions What to watch Alameda County What to watch Contra Costa County What to watch Napa County What to watch San Francisco What to watch San Mateo County What to watch Santa Clara County What to watch Solano County County election offices Key election dates The last day to register to vote for the Nov. 3 general election is Oct. 19. County election officials will start mailing ballots by Oct. 5. Ballot drop-off locations open on Oct. 6 Last day to register to vote for the general election is Oct. 19. First vote centers open for early in-person voting in all Voter’s Choice Act counties on Oct. 24. In person early voting locations in the state open on Oct. 31. Election Day, Nov. 3, is the last day to vote in-person or return a ballot by 8 p.m. Polls will be open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Vote-by-mail ballots must be postmarked no later than Nov. 3. If mailing on election day, get a hand-stamped postmark from a postal employee inside a post office. Visit the California Secretary of State’s website for a full list of key dates and deadlines. Check voter registration status Voters can check their registration at voterstatus.sos.ca.gov to confirm their mailing address and voting status. How to register to vote California residents can register to vote in elections at registertovote.ca.gov. Note Oct. 19 is the last day to register for the general election. Same day voter registration window will be open from Oct. 20 up to the Nov. 3 election day. Visit caearlyvoting.sos.ca.gov for a list of early voting locations to complete same day registration. How to find your polling place Visit the California Secretary of State’s website, where you can input your address to find your polling location and see what is on your ballot. Voters can also visit their county elections office for more information. Scroll down to the Bay Area county election offices section of this guide for further contact information. What to bring to your polling place Voters usually are not required to show identification to a polling place worker before casting a ballot, according to the Secretary of State’s website. There are some instances when providing identification is required: Voting for the first time after registering to vote by mail and did not provide a driver license number California identification number or the last four digits of social security number are missing on registration form In these cases voters should plan to bring identification to a polling place or bring a copy of it with their vote-by-mail ballot. The Secretary of State says the following are acceptable forms of identification: Passport Driver license Official state identification card Student identification card Copy of recent utility bill Sample ballot booklet received from county elections office Any document received by a government agency How to track your mail-in ballot Voters can track their vote-by-mail ballot and confirm it has been received by using the state’s Where’s My Ballot? tool at california.ballottrax.net/voter/. Ballots mailed in may take a few days to appear on the website. Why is California choosing a new governor? Gov. Gavin Newsom terms out after this year and voters will choose between Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton, who both advanced to the general election after a wild primary. Becerra has served as former President Joe Biden’s top health official and oversaw the response to the coronavirus pandemic. He was also the California’s attorney general during President Donald Trump’s first term and has more than two decades of experience as a congressmember. Hilton was a conservative commentator with a show on Fox News for six years. He also worked as an adviser to former British prime minister David Cameron. What are the 14 California propositions voters will decide in the November election? Here’s a list of the California propositions on the November ballot. Use the expandable graphic below for a breakdown on what to know about each measure. 2026 California Ballot Propositions Click on a proposition to see more information about what will happen if it does or doesn’t pass. Source: NBC Staff Reports • Interactive: Annetta Stogniew Regional measure to watch Measure RTM: The Connect Bay Area Transit Initiative, is a regional sales tax aimed at increasing funds for public transit. It includes 5 Bay Area counties: Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo, and Santa Clara. Races and measures to watch in Alameda County California Congressional District 14: California lawmaker Aisha Wahab and Bay Area Rapid Transit Director Melissa Hernandez will face off again to determine who will serve the next full two-year term. Wahab topped Hernandez in an August special election to serve the remainder of former California U.S. Rep. Eric Swalwell’s term. Swalwell resigned from Congress earlier this year after sexual assault and misconduct allegations. District 14 includes the East Bay cities such as Fremont, Hayward and Livermore. Measure X in Berkeley: Would establish 10% limit on annual rent increases and other changes to the city’s rent ordinance. Measure Y in Berkeley: Parcel tax to pay for arts projects. Measure Z in Berkeley: Parcel tax to fund a public bank. Measure AA in Berkeley: Increase soda tax Measure EE in Oakland: Shift city to a strong mayor system. Measure FF in Oakland: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Alameda County and additional election information, visit the Alameda County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Contra Costa County In Contra Costa County, several county board of education seats are open. In Richmond, residents will vote on a new mayor while voters in San Pablo will weigh in on Measure S, which would limit rent increases. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Contra Costa County and additional election information, visit the Contra Costa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Napa County California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. Measure B in Napa County: Sales tax to fund wildfire prevention and open space preservation. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Napa County and additional election information, visit the Napa County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Francisco San Francisco voters will weigh in on several open seats on the county board of supervisors and board of education. Proposition A: Give mayor more power to hire and fire department heads. Proposition B: Pave way for public bank. Proposition C: Increase the city’s annual contribution to an affordable housing trust fund. Proposition D: New barriers to placing measures on the ballot. Proposition E: Changes to city contracting. Proposition G: Reopen parts of the Great Highway to vehicle traffic on weekdays. Proposition H: Parcel tax to fund Muni. Proposition J: Eliminate foreclosure exemption from property transfer tax California Congressional District 11: Scott Wiener and Connie Chan compete to succeed Nancy Pelosi. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Francisco and additional election information, visit the San Francisco Department of Elections website. Races and measures to watch in San Mateo County Measure E in Redwood City: Limit rent increases. Measure Q in Half Moon Bay: Referendum to block proposed farmworker housing. Measure U in San Mateo County: Create independent commission to draw supervisor districts. For a complete list of San Mateo County measures and races on the ballot, visit smacre.gov/elections. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in San Mateo County and additional election information, visit the San Mateo County Elections website. Races and measures to watch in Santa Clara County In San Jose, incumbents Peter Ortiz and Bien Doan are up for re-election in Districts 5 and 7, respectively, and there’s an open seat in District 9. Races and measures to watch in Solano County Solano County Board of Supervisors, District 4: Mike Silva and John Carli face in a runoff in a district covering Vacaville and Dixon. Measure E in Solano County: New tax on data centers and battery storage facilities in the unincorporated county areas. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Solano County and additional election information, visit the Solano County Registrar of Voters website. Races and measures to watch in Sonoma County California Congressional District 1: Mike McGuire will face James Gallagher in a seat redistricted by Proposition 50. California Congressional District 4: Mike Thompson faces Eric Jones. State Assembly District 12: Eric Lucan and Jackie Elward compete in a battle between business and labor. 🗳️ For a complete list of races and measures on the ballot in Sonoma County and additional election information, visit the Sonoma County Registrar of Voters website. headlines.title: Chase Center, bars around the Bay Area filled with Valkyries fans for Game 3
headlines.description: With the Golden State Valkyries playing in Atlanta for Game 3 of the WNBA Finals against the Atlanta Dream, fans in the Bay Area were clamoring for places to watch the game locally alongside other fans. In Game 3, the Valkyries fell to the Dream 71 to 97. The Valks are now down 1 to 2 in the series, which could last as many as 7 games. While the loss was tough for fans to watch, spirits still remain high among the Valkyries’ fanbase. For the first time, the Valkyries hosted a watch party inside their home arena, Chase Center, where fans could watch the game on the big screens inside. Typically, the team hosts free watch parties at the Thrive City Plaza just outside of Chase Center, where fans can sit on lawn chairs or the steps of the plaza. But for this game, the team tried something new and charged fans $25 for tickets. The Valkyries said the net proceeds of the event go to the Golden State Community Foundation, which supports education and youth development programs in the Bay Area. Victor Johnson, who traveled with his mom from Hayward to attend the watch party, felt the $25 entrance fee was “very reasonable,” noting they have paid as much as $400 for tickets to attend Valkyries games at Chase Center before. “Why not come to something that’s cheaper, and the proceeds are going to a good cause,” Johnson said. The crowd filled up most of the lower bowl sections in the arena from Section 111 through 119. Fans were given rally towels, and many brought their own signs, costumes, and purple wigs to wear. Some of the concession booths were open, so fans could order food and drinks. The crowd got some help driving the energy up from Valkyries’ emcee Ari Waller, Valkyries’ DJ Shellheart, “The Flock” dance crew, and Valkyries’ spunky mascot, Violet. Michelle made the trip from her home in Pleasant Hill to enjoy the watch party, saying, “After Game 2, I think [the Valkyries] needed a little bit more support tonight, so I’m here, got my pom poms, I’m with my fans, let’s go baby!” Watch parties happened across the Bay Area, including at many sports bars and restaurants. At Spark Social in San Jose, Kim attended the watch party with her wife and daughter. Kim said of Valkyries’ games, “It’s just become so much a part of our lives.” She continued, “for me as somebody who was never into sports, we love the positivity the Valkyries fans bring, and we’re really are just excited, we’re rooting for them, we want them to win.” At Rikki’s Sports Bar in San Francisco, which prioritizes women’s sports, the bar was at capacity yet again, with crowds waiting in line out the door to watch Game 3. “I don’t usually go out on a weeknight, but it’s kind of a big deal,” said Kay Sirota of Oakland of the Valkyries’ historic playoff run in their second season. While fans were disappointed with the outcome of game three, they still believe their team has what it takes to be league champions. “There’s a lot of basketball left, I keep telling my wife, ‘it’s best of seven, best of seven,’” Sirota said. Game 4 will also be played in Atlanta, it starts at 10 a.m. Pacific Time on Saturday. Chase Center will be hosting another ticketed watch party inside the arena. Many local sports bars will be airing the game, including those that are part of the Valkyries’ official Bar Network.

headlines.title: Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 for a 2-1 lead in the WNBA Finals
headlines.description: Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream are halfway toward their ultimate goal of winning the franchise’s first WNBA championship. They know there is still work to do. But with a huge Atlanta crowd behind them and Reese dominating the last two games, there’s reason to believe in a team that never even had a WNBA Finals win until this series. Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds to help the Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 on Wednesday night and take a 2-1 lead. It was the second straight strong game for Reese, who had 30 points and 16 rebounds in Game 2, which the Dream also won for their first victory ever in the championship round. She has a double-double in each game of the finals. “It feels good when you’re in the finals. It’s a long season and you play against everybody and go through and push through, but when you can do it at the highest level, this is what you live for, this is what the offseason is for,” Reese said. “I put the work in for this moment and I’m just happy I could lead the team to a win. We’re feeling good going into Saturday.” That game will also be played at State Farm Arena. Both games in Atlanta were originally set for the Gateway Center Arena, where the Dream play most of their home games. The league was able to work with the Atlanta Hawks to play Games 3 and 4 there so that they could have a much bigger crowd. Gateway only seats 3,500. State Farm Arena can seat more than 17,000 fans. And they made a difference. “Protect home court,” said Atlanta’s Rhyne Howard, who had 16 points and five steals. “Giving our fans a show. We fought for this arena so we had to protect it. It’s big. We went and stole one but we can’t let them come in and do the same thing.” With the game tied at 49 in the third quarter, Atlanta scored eight straight, including four by Reese. Golden State got within 59-55 on Tiffany Hayes’ layup, but could get no closer as Atlanta closed the quarter scoring 12 of the final 14 points. “I’m most proud of the second half because the first few possessions were a little sloppy. I was really close to using a timeout. They pulled together on their own and got it worked out, cleaned it up themselves,” Atlanta coach Karl Smesko said. “They knew what mistakes they were making, and they huddled up. And then they started making plays, and it started. The crowd started getting behind it.” Atlanta has dominated the third quarter so far in the series, outscoring Golden State 63-35 combined in the three games. With Atlanta up 17 in the fourth quarter, Jordin Canada overthrew Reese on the break, but she saved the ball by throwing it over her head underneath the basket to Howard, who got fouled. Golden State could never recover. Gabby Williams scored 15 points and Hayes added 14 for the Valkyries. “Disappointed in our fight. This game they wanted it more than us,” Hayes said. “That’s not who we are, who we’ve been and how we got here.” Wednesday night’s game was sold out, as is Game 4 on Saturday. The crowd included many music stars, including Ludacris. Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom said he was going to be at the game. The Atlanta Dream and State Farm Arena offered him a private suite for his protection. He refused to sit in it and left the arena. The game got off to a slow start as Atlanta led 9-1 after the first five minutes. Golden State missed its first eight shots before Aminata Gueye scored the first basket for the Valkyries with 4:39 left. They got within 13-10 before Naz Hillmon hit consecutive 3-pointers and then Reese hit one. The Dream led 23-15 after the opening quarter. The hot 3-point shooting continued in the second quarter as Atlanta built its lead to 37-26 midway through the period. Golden State was able to hang around and only trailed 46-40 at the break as the teams combined to shoot 15-for-31 (48%) from behind the arc. That was more made 3-pointers in the first 20 minutes then in either Game 1 or Game 2. Reese had 15 points and WNBA Sixth Woman of the Year Janelle Salaun had 11 for the Valkyries. Game 1 and 2 had huge ratings with the opener on NBC averaging 2.1 million, the most ever to watch a first game of the Finals. Game 2, which was broadcast on USA Network, averaged 1.33 million viewers. ___ See AP’s full WNBA coverage here

headlines.title: San Francisco health officials report city's first deadly overdose involving MGM-15
headlines.description: San Francisco health officials are warning about the city’s first reported deadly overdose involving a powerful new opioid. It comes as police announce the seizure of hundreds of kratom-related products from city smoke shops. A product that looks like an ordinary supplement is now the focus of a deadly overdose warning. San Francisco health officials say a person died in late September in the city’s first reported fatal overdose involving MGM-15. Forensic researcher Dr. Alex Krotulski, who studies emerging drugs, says consumers may not know what they’re taking. “The more common thing is that products are sold under more sort of generic terms, like roprietary blend,” he said. “A majority of people using MGM-15 won’t know they’re being exposed to it.” MGM-15 is a powerful opioid derived from kratom-related compounds. Krotulski compares its potency to morphine. Federal officials have temporarily placed it in Schedule 1, making unauthorized sales and possession Illegal. “It is also possible the person selling it didn’t know that they were selling it because it exists in a shadow in a world sort of legality and illegality,” Krotulski said. In separate investigations, San Francisco police searched two smoke shops: one on Haight Street on Sept. 10 and another on Geary Boulevard on Oct. 9. More than 400 kratom products were seized from the Geary location. Police have not reported finding MGM-15 at either shop or linked them to the death. Supervisor Bilal Mahmood, who represents the Haight, says the overdose death heightens his concerns about dangerous products being sold locally. He also praises police for their recent seizures. “I appreciate that we’re working really fast to address this and we’re going to work collaboratively across different city departments to ensure we contain this as best as we can,” Mahmood said. Health officials are urging consumers to be cautious with products that don’t clearly list their ingredients.

headlines.title: UC Berkeley students rally in support of Prop 40 amid growing opposition
headlines.description: There was a big rally for the so-called Billionaire’s Tax at UC Berkeley, which is backed by a Bay Area congressman. At the same time, the opposition to the measure is mounting and could make history. Prop 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on more than 200 billionaires in California. Proponents say that money would go primarily towards healthcare, with some reserved for food assistance and education. At a UC Berkeley rally in support of the proposition, Representative Ro Khanna, one of the measure’s most vocal supporters, took the stage. “It works because it raises the billions of dollars that will be needed so 3.5 million Californians don’t lose health care,” he said. He says it’s because the Trump administration cut tens of billions from Medi-Cal, which provides health insurance to low-income people, and now threatens hospitals and clinics. But the opposition against Prop 40 is massive, and so is the spending against it. Groups opposed have spent a combined $88.7 million on ads through the election, according to the ad-tracking firm AdImpact. “You see ads not only opposing Prop 40 but also for Prop 41 and Prop 42, those two measures on the ballot to nullify proposition 40,” KQED political correspondent Guy Marzorati said. “I think the big question at this point, given all the money that’s going against Prop 40, where does it end up in history?” For now, Governor Newsom opposes the proposed tax and backs Prop 42. “Gavin Newsom thinks that’s a bad idea. Because he needs those billionaire donors to run his presidential campaign,” Prop 40 supporter Saikat Chakrabarti said. NBC Bay Area reached out to the governor’s office but did not hear back. The chairman of the Silicon Valley GOP Dave Johnson argues the state could lose out on the taxes they would’ve gotten from billionaires if this passes. “If you kill the engine which in other words those billionaires are typically entrepreneurs of they have established companies if you tax them even a one-time tax they could just move to another state and take their employees with them,” he said. Johnson adds the cuts to Medi-Cal is returning things back to the way it was. “When the federal government says we’re going to cut off your revenue stream the state cries wolf and says it’s all his fault it’s all fault never admitting that they are the reason that the federal government had to do that,” he said.

headlines.title: Halloween props stolen from San Leandro family's home
headlines.description: A San Leandro family says thieves have taken two of the props that help make their home a neighborhood attraction. They said this is the second year in a row they’ve been hit. For 20 years, the Nuttings have been turning their home into a Halloween destination. First in Oakland, now in San Leandro. They have a new theme every year, homemade props, store-bought animatronics and free walkthroughs that bring the neighborhood right into the action. But this weekend, two of their biggest props disappeared. “On this side of the house that doesn’t, or didn’t have a camera rather, two major props were stolen, one was a brand new one, and one was a senior veteran prop,” D.W. Nutting said. The family says the two animatronics cost hundreds of dollars. They’ve since installed a camera to cover that side of the house and said this isn’t the first time they’ve been targeted. Last year, surveillance video captured someone in a red hoodie running off with one of their decorations. It’s a problem other homeowners say they’ve faced, too. For the Nuttings, the loss isn’t just about the money. “It’s very disheartening because we know that a lot of people enjoy it, a lot of people respect what we do, we bring a lot of joy,” D.W. Nutting said. Neighbors on NextDoor say their children and grandchildren love coming by to see the display. And for the family, that’s the whole point: creating something people can enjoy together, and a tradition their children can carry on. The family has started an online fundraiser to help replace the stolen props and finish this year’s display. NBC Bay Area reached out to San Leandro police to ask whether they’ve received reports of other decoration thefts but did not hear back.

headlines.title: Livermore Valley named Wine Region of the Year
headlines.description: The Livermore Valley was just named “Wine Region of the Year,” one of a handful of designations given out by Wine Enthusiast, which is a well-known publication in the industry. Wine Enthusiast recognized Livermore for its multi-generational wineries and its small family operations experimenting with lesser-known grapes. The Livermore Valley is one of California’s oldest wine regions and home to about 50 wineries. Over the past few years, these wineries have adapted to the times by focusing more on hospitality and marketing.
